MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 23, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on June 23, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 19, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CONSIDERATION OF ADDITION OF LATE ARISING MATTER

City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt announced a request to add a Closed Session item for one four-part
item as the need arose after the agenda was posted and there is a need to take immediate action
regarding City Representation of Legal Services: Public Employee Appointment, Public
Employment, Public Employee Performance Evaluation, and Public Employee Discipline/
Dismissal/Release: City Attorney position.
City Council Minutes  1  June 23, 2020
 Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to add a Closed
Session item for one four-part item as the need arose after the agenda was posted and there is a need
to take immediate action regarding City Representation of Legal Services: Public Employee
Appointment, Public Employment, Public Employee Performance Evaluation, and Public
Employee Discipline/Dismissal/Release: City Attorney position.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Outlined specific letters from the Secretary of State to the City
  regarding cumulative voting. She questioned the City’s withdrawal from the amicus brief
  and restated that everyone should be fired.

CS2. City Representation of Legal Services: Public Employee Appointment, Public
  Employment, Public Employee Performance Evaluation, and Public Employee
  Discipline/Dismissal/ Release: City Attorney position.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:14 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

For CS1. City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the plaintiffs have agreed, by mutual decision,
with the City of Mission Viejo to ask the court to continue the stipulated judgement, in essence to
push it down the road for two years. This election will be as the City is used to, there will be two
seats up that are now occupied by the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for two-year terms. He stated
that there has been a stipulated decision between the parties, good faith is demonstrated and the
Court should have no difficulty embracing the decision. Mr. Curley noted that he is in touch with
the plaintiff’s legal counsel on a regular basis along with other interested parties. Lastly, he restated
that the 2020 election will be in the normal format with two seats for a two-year term and the
remaining Council Members will have a four-year term until 2022.

For CS2, the Closed Session item that was added, City Manager Dennis Wilberg announced that
the Council gave direction to staff but there is no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

City Council Minutes  2  June 23, 2020
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Kraig Erickson, M.V.: Commented on the property adjacent to the Casta del Sol Golf Course,
extension of the Oso Trail, and the City’s Bikeway Master Plan implementation. He voiced concern
with the funding of these projects and reminded the Council and staff of the CIP prioritization list
that was recommended by the Community Services Commission in April. Mr. Erickson suggested
that the Council re-engage with the Commission on evaluating the impact of those CIP projects to
ensure prior promises and direction are maintained.

Irma Youssefieh, M.V.: Asked for clarification on the Golf Course Naming Contest in regards to
the number of submissions per household.

Public Law Center: Asked that the City suspend enforcement of pending eviction orders that are
due to COVID-19.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the Council for not holding open meetings in the Council Chamber
since surrounding cities have opened up. She said the Council does not wish to hear the voices of
the public and that the public will remember come November 3.

Tommie Kozlov, M.V., Catherine Palmer, M.V., and Bonnie Eastman, M.V.: Questioned what
type of election the City intends to hold, what are the filing dates for those wishing to run for a City
Council seat, and when will the paperwork be available on the City’s website.

The following commented on police defunding, police reform, police budget, and the Black Lives
Matter movement: Dr. Sharareh Frouzesh, M.V., Grace Mortero, M.V.; Shane Yamada; Lauren
Sanford, M.V.; Gabe Reyes, Canyon Crest; Kelly Stack; Mary Stack, M.V.; D. Cau; Erin Mallon,
M.V.; Shelbi Richardson, M.V.; Olivia Medina; Sarah Manely, Ladera Ranch; Leah Atkins, Galicia
South; Arya Jemal, M.V.; Cameron Lopez; Sarah Lasker, M.V.; Melissa Bader-Huesgen; Liv Orea;
Whitney Azizi, and Brandon Rotkel.

Joe Monroe, Jessica Monroe, and J. Monroe: Expressed their concern with any proposal to defund
police.

Robert Breton, M.V.: Encouraged the City Council to adopt the resolution approving the CDBG
5-Year Consolidated Plan and thanked Director Elaine Lister and Consultant Mike Linares for their
outstanding omnibus report.

The Kennedy Commission: Recommended that the City allocate a portion of CDBG funds for
activities that address the housing/service needs of the elderly and lower-income households as well
as promoting and preserving affordable housing.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  3  June 23, 2020
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 23, 2020, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated May 29, 2020 in the Amount of $300,833.36

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated June 5, 2020 in the Amount of $891,996.79

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  FY 2020/21 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 20-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2020/21 Fiscal Year.

5.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget - Fiscal Year 2020/21

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 20-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority (MVHA) for FY 2020/21.

6.  2020 Residential Resurfacing - Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 21838)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Onyx Paving Company,
  Inc.(A20-12) in the amount of $786,000.00; and (2) adopted Resolution 20-18 Amending the
  Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Budget for Costs Related to CIP 20838.

7.  Professional Services Consultant Team

  (1) Approved the Professional Services Consultant Team Roster (for plan check/design or
  other professional services); (2) authorized the City Manager to execute contracts with
  members of the Professional Services Consultant Team as needed; (3) authorized the City
  Manager to add consultants to the Professional Services Consultant Team Roster as needed
  during the contract term

8.  Authorization Resolution for Application of the Local Early Action Planning (LEAP)
  Grants Program, for Purchase of a New Permit Tracking Software for the Community
  Development Department

  Adopted Resolution 20-19 Authorizing Application for, and Receipt of, Local Early Action
  Planning Grants Program Funds.

City Council Minutes  4  June 23, 2020
 9.  2020 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 21838) - Slurry Seal

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer, and
  authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

10. Draft 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan, including the 2020-2021 Annual Action Plan
  Detailing the Proposed Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds,
  and the 2020-2024 Orange County Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice

  Adopted Resolution 20-20 approving the City's 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan including the
  2020-2021 Annual Action Plan detailing the proposed use of Community Development Block
  Grant Funds, and the 2020-2024 Orange County Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing
  Choice, and authorizing submission of such plans to the United States Department of Housing
  and Urban Development.

11. Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center Flooring Rehabilitation

  Awarded a contract to Shaw Industries, Inc. DBA Shaw Integrated Solutions (A20-13) in an
  amount not to exceed $159,448.10 to replace the flooring at the Norman P. Murray
  Community and Senior Center.

12. Microsoft & Azure Cloud Licensing Renewal

  Approved agreement and issue purchase order to SoftwareONE (A20-14) for year three of
  three-year Microsoft agreement for software licensing in the amount of $107,282.22 including
  a 10% contingency.

13. Annual City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M2 FY2020/21 Eligibility Submittal
  Requirements to the Orange County Transportation Authority

  Adopted Resolution 20-21 Concerning the 2020 Update of the Local Signal Synchronization
  Plan, the Status and Update of the 2020 Pavement Management Plan, and Adoption of the
  Measure M (M2) Seven-Year Capital Improvement Program beginning with the 2020/2021
  fiscal year, in order to maintain eligibility for funding through the Orange County Measure M
  (M2) Program.

14. Fiscal Year 2020/21 Senate Bill 1 Road Repair and Accountability Act

  Adopted Resolution 20-22 Adopting a List of Projects for Fiscal Year 2020/21 Funded by
  Senate Bill 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017.

15. First Amendment to Conditional Agreement for Removal of Offer of Dedication
  (Irrevocable)

  Approved First Amendment to Conditional Agreement with Saddleback Valley Church.

16. Continuing Appropriations Authorization Commencing July 1, 2020

City Council Minutes  5  June 23, 2020
   Adopted Resolution 20-23 Authorizing Appropriations Commencing July 1, 2020.

17. Contract Renewal with Mercy House Living Centers for Homeless Outreach Services

  Approved Mercy House Living Centers Contract (A20-15) for Homeless Outreach Services.

OLD BUSINESS

18. COVID-19 Update

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the report.

19. Request of Three Homeowners Association Board of Directors to Manage Pest Control
  by All Authorized means, Including Firearms

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Carole Weidler, M.V.: Commented in favor of the variance in Casta de Sol.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  (1) approve the request of Casta Del Sol Homeowners Association for a variance that will
  allow the association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible
  for the health, safety and welfare of the community; (2) approve the request of Mission Viejo
  Environmental Association for a variance that will allow the association to manage on-site
  nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for the health, safety and welfare of the
  community; and (3) approve the request of Palmia Masters Association for a variance that
  will allow the association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means
  possible for the health, safety and welfare of the community.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

20. Integrated Solid Waste Management Services

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that the purchase of the golf course has made the City cash poor.
  She expressed concern with the street sweeping contract no longer being paid out of the
  general fund and said that adding the cost to the trash bill will cause an additional tax to
  residents.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Asked the Council to remove the street sweeping costs from the Waste
  Management agreement. He questioned if residents living in gated communities will receive
  the same solid waste removal increase for their streets which are not covered by this contract.
City Council Minutes  6  June 23, 2020
   MVballer16, M.V.: Stated that the change in street sweeping responsibilities from the City’s
  general fund to residents’ trash collection bill is an excellent idea.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 20-24 Awarding a Franchise Agreement for Integrated Solid Waste
  Management Services to Waste Management Collection and Recycling Inc., dba Waste
  Management of Orange County (A20-16) for the period from January 1, 2021, through
  December 31, 2028; and (2) authorize the approval of Contract Change Order 2 for Solid
  Waste and Recycling Consulting Services in the amount of $12,915 to Sloan Vazquez
  McAfee.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

21. Two Month Extension of Mission Viejo Nadadores Financial Relief due to the Covid-19
  Outbreak

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)
  approve an additional 1-month extension (June 2020) fee waiver for utility
  expenses, (2) provide a total of a 5-month deferment on the Funding Agreement
  rehabilitation loan for a revised length of 245 months, (3) continue to reimburse for routine
  pool maintenance (June and July) and, (4) continue to provide daily janitorial services to meet
  the required COVID-19 State Mandates until December 31, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

22. General Municipal Election - November 3, 2020

  City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt presented the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the City Council and City Attorney for their decision to
  extend the terms of the Council. She questioned the legality and asked where in the Election
  Code this power or authority is given.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Questioned the transparency of the Council as it relates to the November
  2020 General Election. He asked that the Council vote no on the resolutions calling the

City Council Minutes  7  June 23, 2020
   election and regulations pertaining to candidate statements. Mr. Gilbert reminded the Council
  that the Secretary of State has not agreed to draft of sponsor any legislation related to
  alternative voting systems.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to (1) adopt
  Resolution 20-25 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to be Held on
  Tuesday, November 3, 2020, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required by the
  Provisions of the Laws of the State of California Relating to General Law Cities; (2) adopt
  Resolution 20-27 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange to
  Consolidate a General Municipal Election to be Held on November 3, 2020, with the
  Statewide General Election to be Held on the Same Date pursuant to § 10403 of the Elections
  Code; (3) adopt Resolution 20-26 Adopting Regulations for Candidates for Elective Officer
  Pertaining to Candidate Statements Submitted to the Voters at an Election to be Held on
  November 3, 2020; and (4) direct the City Clerk to schedule the adoption of the resolution
  citing the election results and administration of the oath to the newly elected Council Members
  on December 8, 2020, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

23. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

24. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

25. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum asked staff to explain what residents can and cannot do along the streets
during the July 4th Fireworks show since there will not be a Street Faire. She also asked staff to
publicize the do’s and don’ts on the City’s website. She expressed concern with crowds since
neighboring cities are not having a fireworks show and noted that there may be an influx of people.
Council Member Bucknum suggested that the Council, at a future meeting, discuss the idea of
City Council Minutes  8  June 23, 2020
 conducting a poll of the residents regarding their opinion on the investment the City makes in public
safety. She encouraged residents to be patient and noted that the City is taking precautions for the
community and staff before opening Council Meetings to the public. Lastly, Council Member
Bucknum wished everyone a Happy 4th of July.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the Mayor and staff for putting together the virtual meetings and
said that he hopes to be back in the Council Chamber in July. He stated, for the record, that he will
never vote to defund police and that Orange County Sheriff’s Department is doing a fantastic job
keeping the community safe.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs commended the Mayor for the job he is doing under these extraordinary
circumstances. He voiced concern with misinformed community members that do not understand
how Mission Viejo is policed and how deputies are trained. Council Member Sachs also noted that
he has met many people in the public that do not want to defund the police. He reminded residents
that the City has always had a balanced budget. Council Member Sachs addressed specific questions
from one of the public comments read earlier, he outlined the benefits of Secure OC Schools and
he defended his position on the program. In closing, Council Member Sachs stated that he will not
vote to defund the police and thus put in jeopardy the safety of the residents of the City. He said it
is the primary responsibility of government to protect its citizens.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commended Council Member Sachs on his clarification and truth about the
public comment that was presented this evening regarding police services. She gave kudos to staff
who have kept the City running during these turbulent times. She also addressed the trash contract
and clarified that the monthly fees will go up to $21.78 per month effective January 2021 and that
the majority of the increase is due to legislation from Sacramento. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
announced that the Library is offering curbside pick-up and the recreation pools are open for lap
swimming only. She said she is hopeful the pools will open for recreation swimming soon. Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley said that the City is watching out for the safety of its residents and the City Council
meetings will be open when it is safe. She noted that she donated blood yesterday, along with
Mayor Goodell, and she thanked volunteer Rebecca Moore for managing the check-in table. Lastly,
she expressed her gratitude to Police Services staff, the Deputies and the Sergeants for going above
and beyond. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley reminded the public to let the police hear their gratitude for
their work in keeping Mission Viejo safe and maintaining the status as one of the top 10 safest cities
in the Nation for many years.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell commented on the public comment regarding defunding the police. He explained
that the City funds six School Resource Officers (SROs) and he feels that those SROs are a critical
link to people in need in the community, especially the students in the City’s schools. He clarified
that the police budget was lower than last year and that the City did not add $500,000 to the Police
Services budget as was mentioned in several public comments. Mayor Goodell commended
Council Member Sachs for his Secure OC Schools Program. He too mentioned that he donated his
City Council Minutes  9  June 23, 2020
 plasma yesterday at the blood drive and encouraged residents to donate as well. He also noted that
for a limited time, the American Red Cross is conducting an antibody test on donors’ blood to find
out if that person has been exposed to the COVID-19 virus. Mayor Goodell stated that the Economic
Development Committee has been reviewing proposals for the Golf Course Vision Plan and will
have a report at the next meeting on July 14. Lastly, he wished everyone a Happy 4 th of July.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:14 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 14, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 14, 2020

City Council Minutes  10  June 23, 2020
